world.summary: Restored world-sea-001's snapshot (509e888; every restored path is owned), then fixed findings 1-8. (1) sail-and-dock now samples real canvas pixels (15x15 tile interiors via data-camera) at a Palm Key land tile, a shoal-bar tile, Palm Key's west dock and a sea tile, and expects each tile's placeholder colour. The palette moved into the Phaser-free apps/web/src/palette.ts so the tests use the scene's own constants. (2) The same scenario waits until the ship is drawn at its start, records data-fog-revealed, finds the open-sea tiles near the route that are still fog-coloured on the minimap (the scene now reports its geometry in data-minimap), then requires the count to rise leg by leg and every one of those minimap pixels to turn to sea. (3) dockInReach requires hullPathIsClear along the straight run to the berth, checked one sub-unit at a time. A unit test covers a diagonal land-corner cut, a clear straight run and a shoal mid-segment. (4) protocol PLACEMENT_HEADING_COUNT replaces the hard-coded max(63); apps/server/src/testPlacement.test.ts ties it to content HEADING_COUNT, and the protocol tests use it. (5) seaValidation derives its octile costs from map.subUnitsPerTile with an integer square root (octileStepCosts). A unit test checks several scales and shows that half the scale gives exactly half the costs. (6) smoke-build imports TEST_PLACEMENT_PATH. (7) apps/server/package.json has a literal § again. (8) HeadlessClient throws a clear error if room.connection.events.onmessage is missing, and a comment names @colyseus/sdk 0.18.4. docs/architecture.md's docking line now mentions the clear-run check. Checks run after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), test:unit (135 passed), test:integration (21 passed), npm run build including the smoke test (passed), and the full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter (4 passed); check-report reported that all 4 scenarios follow the verifier's rules. Mutation checks: with the tile layer not drawn, the land-tile assertion failed (share 0). With the minimap not painting revealed tiles, the fog assertion failed (94 candidates still fogged).

The dock-tile colour check uses Palm Key's west dock, not the south dock where the ship moors, because the moored ship's hull and ring cover most of the berth tile.

# Decisions: world-sea-fixes

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, written by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish slices 1 and 2. The run world-sea-001 passed every check, but its coverage reviewer blocked the candidate (P1: the tile map is never proven drawn) and its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict.

## Decisions

- The follow-up starts from the world base (`b8f4c37`) and restores world-sea-001's snapshot (`509e888`, `refs/workflow/e467a18ef3280d1e/world`) as its first step. The reviewers therefore see the whole world diff plus the fixes. That matters here, because no general review of the world code was ever completed. (`skeleton-fixes` instead reviewed only the fixes on top of an already reviewed candidate.)
- Scope: the coverage reviewer's P1 and P2, and six P2s from the assistant's own review of the snapshot (the dock snap sweep, the heading limit, the tile-cost constants, the route literal, the `§` encoding, the SDK-internal guard).
- The map is kept as it is: 224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, neighbours 22–23 s apart, longest crossing 54 s at the skeleton's 5 tiles/s. The emptiness this causes (ships rarely meet with a 10-tile sight radius) is a design question for the next world slice: faster ships or a denser layout.
- The same lane, owned paths, checks and scenario ids as `world-sea`.

## Assumptions

- The assistant's review found no P0 or P1 in the snapshot. A read-only merge of it with `duel-core` (`a23b8a2`) is conflict-free and passes typecheck, unit (228) and integration (21).
- The test-only placement route stays as designed: dev entry only, 404 in production.

## Deferred

- Map density and ship speed, landmarks, the 12-island alpha map.
- Adding the duel subpath exports to `scripts/smoke-build.ts`: done when both branches are merged into `main`.

concerns.message: Finding 1 asks for a pixel at a dock tile in an existing scenario. The natural place is sail-and-dock after docking. But the dock snap puts the ship at the dock centre, and the ship shape covers most of a 16 px tile: a 9 px hull, a bow reaching 17 px and a 13 px ring. The minimap, which the snapshot may draw on the same Phaser canvas, can also cover a sampled tile.
concerns.consequence: The dock sample reads the ship's slot colour or minimap pixels instead of the dock colour. The worker can lose time on flaky or wrong assertions, or pass the check by sampling a pixel that isn't really on the dock. The test should sample a dock tile the ship doesn't cover, or a point away from the ship's footprint, and stay clear of the minimap rectangle.

concerns.message: Tile pixel positions have to come from the content map and the camera scroll. They can't come from scene bookkeeping, or the reviewer's complaint repeats. The expected colours also can't be imported from `apps/web/src/seaScene.ts`, because it imports Phaser at the top and the Playwright spec runs in Node. The existing `shipsOnCanvas` helper only works because the scene reports canvas pixel coordinates. The transform from world to screenshot pixels also depends on the scale mode, `roundPixels` and the device pixel ratio.
concerns.consequence: If the spec imports `seaScene.ts`, the whole spec file breaks, all four scenarios with it. If the camera and scale transform is wrong by even half a tile, the samples land on neighbouring sea tiles. The colours belong in a Phaser-free module (or as literals), and the test should sample tile centres with the existing tolerance of 24.

concerns.message: Finding 3 leaves the fix open: sweep the hull along the snap segment, or shrink the dock radius to about one tile. Shrinking the radius changes behaviour that the browser `sail-and-dock` scenario relies on, since it docks with keyboard timing, and that integration or unit docking tests may rely on. Sweeping with the existing collision routine keeps the behaviour and only refuses the snaps that cut corners.
concerns.consequence: With a one-tile radius, the keyboard-driven `sail-and-dock` run has to stop within a tile at low speed. That tends to be flaky under 20 Hz patches and real key timing, and it means reworking the scenario route. The sweep is the lower-risk choice.

concerns.message: Finding 4: `@pirate-sea-race/protocol` has no workspace dependencies. `HEADING_COUNT` presumably lives in simulation. To derive the limit inside protocol, the worker would add a protocol→simulation dependency: an edit to `packages/protocol/package.json` and the lockfile, plus a change to build order. Neither the simulation nor the content `package.json` may be touched.
concerns.consequence: A new workspace dependency risks lockfile drift that fails `npm ci`, or a build-order failure in `npm run build`, all for a P2. Simpler: keep the literal and add the unit test where both packages are already dependencies (for example `apps/server`), asserting `max === HEADING_COUNT - 1`.

concerns.message: Finding 7's text reads "rewrote `§` as `§`". Both sides look the same because rendering lost the escape; the file probably contains `§`.
concerns.consequence: A worker reading the task literally may decide there is nothing to change, or grep for the wrong string. It should open `apps/server/package.json` and replace the JSON escape with the literal character.

concerns.message: The decisions record a conflict-free merge with `duel-core` for the snapshot only. The fixes touch `packages/simulation/src/step.ts`, the content validation and `scripts/smoke-build.ts`, and `duel-core-fixes` may be changing shared files at the same time.
concerns.consequence: A fix to the world step or its exports could conflict with, or change the behaviour of, duel code at integration time. The integration approval gate should rerun the read-only merge with current `duel-core` (and `duel-core-fixes`, if it has landed).

challenge.simpler_alternative: Put findings 1 and 2 in one scenario, `sail-and-dock`. Compute the sample points from `seaMap` tile coordinates and the camera scroll, the only value the scene reports. Put the placeholder colours in a Phaser-free module and reuse the existing screenshot-decoding helper. Fix finding 3 by running the existing collision sweep over the snap segment and refusing the dock if the hull isn't clear, not by retuning the dock radius. Fix finding 4 with a test in a package that already depends on both protocol and simulation, not a new workspace dependency.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Restore the snapshot and run only `sail-and-dock`. At the docked moment, save the canvas element screenshot and log the camera scroll. Then read the RGB values at the centres of the nearest land, shoal and dock tiles, computed from `seaMap`. This takes a few minutes and shows whether the transform is right (scale, device pixel ratio, rounding) and whether the docked ship or the minimap covers the chosen tiles, before any assertion is written.

# Task: world

## Goal

Deliver the `world-sea` feature with its review findings fixed. Run world-sea-001 built it and passed every check, but its coverage reviewer blocked the candidate because nothing proves the client draws the tile map, and its general reviewer never finished. Start from that run's snapshot, then close the findings below so that the whole feature can be reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/world-sea/world-task.md` and `features/world-sea/decisions.md` define the feature; all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore world-sea-001's snapshot into your worktree with `git checkout refs/workflow/e467a18ef3280d1e/world -- .` (commit `509e888`). It changes only paths this lane owns. Then read `docs/architecture.md` and the code it describes.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- `duel-core` is already merged on `main`, and `duel-core-fixes` may be running. Never create or edit `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, `packages/test-tools/src/replay` or the `package.json` of `simulation`, `content` or `test-tools`. Keep the exports of `hash.ts`, `fixed.ts`, `random.ts`, `frameBudgets.ts` and `rules.ts` (`formatIssues`, `ValidationResult`) unchanged, because the duel code imports them.

Findings to fix:

1. (coverage, P1) No test checks that the web client draws the tile map. `SeaScene.createTerrain` (`apps/web/src/seaScene.ts`, around lines 97–141) is never read back, and the browser helpers sample pixels only at ship positions. Add browser assertions (in an existing scenario, keeping the scenario ids) that sample canvas pixels at a known land, shoal and dock tile, using the camera offset, and expect each tile's placeholder colour.
2. (coverage, P2) The browser check for fog is weak: `data-fog-revealed` is checked once at spawn and comes from the scene's own bookkeeping. Show in a scenario that the revealed count grows as the ship sails, and that a revealed minimap pixel changes from the fog colour.
3. (P2) The dock snap (`packages/simulation/src/step.ts`, around line 46) moves the ship straight to the dock centre without the collision sweep and can cut a diagonal corner. Require a clear hull along the segment, or shrink the dock radius to about one tile; test it.
4. (P2) `packages/protocol/src/testPlacement.ts` hard-codes `max(63)` for the heading. Tie it to `HEADING_COUNT - 1` with a unit test (or derive it).
5. (P2) `packages/content/src/seaValidation.ts` hard-codes 256 and 362 per tile. Derive the costs from `map.subUnitsPerTile`.
6. (P2) `scripts/smoke-build.ts` repeats the route literal `/__test/place`. Import `TEST_PLACEMENT_PATH`.
7. (P2) `apps/server/package.json` rewrote `§` as `§`. Restore the literal character.
8. (P2) `packages/test-tools/src/headlessClient.ts` wraps an internal of the Colyseus SDK (`room.connection.events.onmessage`). Guard it with an assertion that fails clearly if the hook is missing, and note the SDK version it depends on.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need, and keep the existing structure, names and patterns.
- Keep the map, its scale and the travel times as they are. The map's large empty sea is a known design issue for the next world slice, not for this task.
- Keep the four browser scenario ids and the protocol version (3).

## Acceptance

- The restored `world-sea` feature meets all of `features/world-sea/world-task.md`'s acceptance.
- Findings 1–8 are fixed. Finding 1 asserts real canvas pixels at land, shoal and dock tiles. Finding 2 shows fog clearing along a sailed path on the minimap. Findings 3–5 have unit tests.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

completion.summary: Restored world-sea-001's snapshot (509e888; every restored path is owned), then fixed findings 1-8. (1) sail-and-dock now samples real canvas pixels (15x15 tile interiors via data-camera) at a Palm Key land tile, a shoal-bar tile, Palm Key's west dock and a sea tile, and expects each tile's placeholder colour. The palette moved into the Phaser-free apps/web/src/palette.ts so the tests use the scene's own constants. (2) The same scenario waits until the ship is drawn at its start, records data-fog-revealed, finds the open-sea tiles near the route that are still fog-coloured on the minimap (the scene now reports its geometry in data-minimap), then requires the count to rise leg by leg and every one of those minimap pixels to turn to sea. (3) dockInReach requires hullPathIsClear along the straight run to the berth, checked one sub-unit at a time. A unit test covers a diagonal land-corner cut, a clear straight run and a shoal mid-segment. (4) protocol PLACEMENT_HEADING_COUNT replaces the hard-coded max(63); apps/server/src/testPlacement.test.ts ties it to content HEADING_COUNT, and the protocol tests use it. (5) seaValidation derives its octile costs from map.subUnitsPerTile with an integer square root (octileStepCosts). A unit test checks several scales and shows that half the scale gives exactly half the costs. (6) smoke-build imports TEST_PLACEMENT_PATH. (7) apps/server/package.json has a literal § again. (8) HeadlessClient throws a clear error if room.connection.events.onmessage is missing, and a comment names @colyseus/sdk 0.18.4. docs/architecture.md's docking line now mentions the clear-run check. Checks run after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), test:unit (135 passed), test:integration (21 passed), npm run build including the smoke test (passed), and the full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter (4 passed); check-report reported that all 4 scenarios follow the verifier's rules. Mutation checks: with the tile layer not drawn, the land-tile assertion failed (share 0). With the minimap not painting revealed tiles, the fog assertion failed (94 candidates still fogged).
open_assumptions: PLACEMENT_HEADING_COUNT is a protocol constant tied to content's HEADING_COUNT by a server unit test, not derived by import. The protocol package does not depend on content, and adding that dependency would change the package graph and the lockfile.
The dock snap keeps the 1.5-tile dock radius and adds the clear-hull check (the first option in finding 3) instead of shrinking the radius.
The dock-tile colour check uses Palm Key's west dock, not the south dock where the ship moors, because the moored ship's hull and ring cover most of the berth tile.
untested: The fog check depends on the placement jump (drawn as a glide from the random spawn slot) leaving at least one candidate tile fogged. A worst-case calculation says one always remains, but no run has exercised the north or north-east spawn slot on purpose.
Pixel colours are checked only under the headless Chromium renderer that Playwright uses, not in other browsers or GPUs.
